clue.text: Stopping assistant showing fracture to an audience — dead strange

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound and not its spelling

blocks.note: a fracture is a break; said out loud it matches a word spelt differently
D is the standard abbreviation for dead
rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: Someone describes a helper with a broken bone, adding that it was all very peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: BREAK sounds like BRAKE, then D + RUM gives DRUM. 'Rum' meaning odd is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake drum is the rotating part of a vehicle braking system that helps bring wheels to a halt.

clue.text: In the House of Lords, official support staff to take Latin

definitions.text: In the House of Lords, official

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to back is to support
L is the abbreviation for Latin
a staff is a rod or stick

explanation.surface: A description of back-office staff in the House of Lords being sent off to study Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support staff' looks like one phrase meaning back-office workers, but it splits in two, and 'support' wraps around the Latin letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Black Rod is the ceremonial officer of the House of Lords, famous for knocking on the Commons door at the State Opening of Parliament.

clue.text: Cheeky, exposed backside in Boston

indicators.note: exposed means with its covering stripped off, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: sassy means impudent or cheeky

explanation.surface: A cheeky streaker bares their bottom on the streets of Boston.
explanation.walkthrough: SASSY loses its first and last letters. 'In Boston' marks the American spelling: the British would say arse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ass is the American slang word for buttocks, the counterpart of British arse.

clue.text: Reputation of artist consequently dropping hard

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is lost from the word

blocks.note: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist
hence means as a result
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard; it is the letter taken away

explanation.surface: An artist's standing collapses as a result of giving up hard work, or hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: EMIN + HENCE without its H gives EMINENCE. Tracey Emin is a British artist best known for her unmade bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is fame or distinguished standing, a close synonym of a good reputation.

clue.text: After scratching head, understand file

indicators.note: scratching out the head means striking off the first letter

blocks.note: to grasp an idea is to understand it

explanation.surface: Someone scratches their head in puzzlement before finally making sense of a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' looks like a document, but it is the tool. GRASP loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse metalworking or woodworking tool, a type of file with raised teeth.

clue.text: Nasty man aggressive; I must leave

indicators.note: whatever must leave is dropped out of the word

blocks.note: a man is a male
aggressive behaviour can be violent
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone facing a threatening man decides they had better get out.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE + VIOLENT, with the I taken out. The 'I' in the surface is the speaker; in the wordplay it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Malevolent means wishing harm on others, so it is a stronger synonym for spiteful or unpleasant.

clue.text: Papers in a row, relatively neat

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: ID papers are identity documents
a tier is a row, as in theatre seating

explanation.surface: Papers stacked in a line look fairly orderly on a desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A row' is a tier, and ID goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative form of tidy describes something more orderly than another, which is what 'relatively' asks for.

clue.text: How to get lots of admirers hammered

definitions.text: How to get lots of admirers

blocks.clueFragment: How to get lots of admirers
blocks.note: first meaning, read in three words: be rated ten out of ten for looks
second meaning: struck repeatedly, or thrashed in a contest

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as BE A TEN: being a perfect ten wins admirers. 'Hammered' also suggests drunk, but here it means struck or defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that has been hammered has been beaten into shape, and a side that is hammered is soundly defeated.

clue.text: Sound of sneeze under discussion

indicators.note: a sound is something heard, so the word is taken by how it is said

blocks.note: atishoo is the British written form of the noise of a sneeze

explanation.surface: A meeting interrupted by someone's sneeze while a topic is being debated.
explanation.walkthrough: Atishoo is how British comics spell a sneeze (Americans write achoo); said aloud it matches the two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being debated or disputed, so it is currently being talked over.

clue.text: Damaged seat on British motor car that can be very noisy

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing in for the noun 'thing that can be very noisy'

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Morgan is a small British maker of hand-built sports cars

explanation.surface: A complaint about a ripped seat in a British car with a loud engine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. The definition is the whole closing clause: something that can be very noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam organ is a loud fairground instrument powered by steam pipes, often heard across a whole fair.

clue.text: Coordinate muscles, so taken aback by onset of spasms

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word is written from end to start
the onset is the start, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: abs are abdominal muscles
sic is Latin for thus or so
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Coordinating your muscles proves difficult when cramps set in unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coordinate' looks like a verb about muscles; it is the noun from geometry. Absciss is a variant spelling of abscissa.
explanation.definitionFit: The abscissa is the horizontal or x value of a point on a graph, one of its two Cartesian coordinates.

clue.text: Perhaps Trump, Epstein and Andrew repeatedly stripped to get massage

indicators.note: each of the names is stripped bare, losing its outer letters at both ends
to massage is to knead and work over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the name without its first and last letters
the name without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A scandalous picture of three notorious men undressing for a massage.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Epstein was a financier convicted of sex offences and Andrew is the former prince linked to him. Their trimmed names together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump has served as President of the United States, so he is an example of the office holder.

clue.text: Destiny of king is with Eccles, given time

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
Eccles is the setter of this puzzle, so the setter's name stands for ME
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that a king's fate is bound up with theirs, given enough time.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter naming themselves in a clue means ME, the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is a word borrowed from Turkish via Arabic for fate or a preordained lot in life.

clue.text: Passage that is concerning in songs performed in show

indicators.note: being in something means placed inside it

blocks.note: id est is the Latin phrase abbreviated to i.e., meaning that is
re means about or concerning
a set is the list of songs a band plays at a gig

explanation.surface: A reviewer worries about one section of the songs in a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' is usually IE; here it is the full Latin, ID EST. 'Passage' sounds like a piece of music but is a narrow street.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage can be a narrow way or alley between buildings, and a minor road is a similar thoroughfare.

clue.text: Heart broken by politician, man with need on vacation to make out

indicators.note: something broken by an intruder is split open with that intruder inside
a vacated word is emptied, keeping only its outside letters

blocks.note: the core is the heart of something
MP is a Member of Parliament
he is the pronoun for a man
only the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A heartbroken politician and a needy man on holiday are about to start kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make out' looks like the slang for kissing, which the holiday scene encourages, but it means understand. 'Man' is the pronoun he.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to discern or understand it, the same sense as grasping its meaning.

clue.text: People rowing in boat are dismal fiends, at heart

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the middle pair of this four-letter word
the central letter
the middle pair of this six-letter word
the middle pair of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of a racing crew who are miserable devils at bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People rowing' could mean people arguing; it is the crew in the boat. Four centres in a row build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen are those who pull oars to propel a boat, for instance in a college racing eight.

clue.text: Conservative keeps calm, but Henry shifting a long way to the right

indicators.note: to shift is to move away, so a letter leaves its original place

indicators.text: a long way to the right
indicators.note: moved well rightwards, the letter lands inside a later word rather than at the front

blocks.note: to keep something is to hold it
cool means calm and composed
H is the unit symbol for the henry, of electrical inductance

explanation.surface: A Tory stays composed while a colleague called Henry drifts toward the far right of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLDS COOL, then the H at the front travels rightwards into COOL. 'A long way to the right' sounds political, but it describes the letter moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone old school sticks to traditional ways and resists change, which is the core of conservatism.

clue.text: With injured rib, dawdle in the manner of a newly-wed

definitions.text: in the manner of a newly-wed

indicators.note: an injured thing is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to dally is to dawdle or linger

explanation.surface: A bride with a damaged rib walks slowly up the aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first three letters are shuffled; DALLY follows as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb formed from bridal describes acting like a bride, a woman who has just married.

clue.text: Go before nine, in the end, following a decent cryptic

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured and puzzling, so the letters are disguised by rearrangement
the end is the final position, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice to tackle the crossword before nine o'clock, once you have done a good cryptic.
explanation.walkthrough: The E comes after the rearranged letters, as 'following' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To antecede is to precede, coming earlier in time or order than something else.

clue.text: Quietly finish joke about supreme leader

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to finish is to end
to rag is to tease or play a joke on
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly wraps up a joke about the country's dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a reversal or container signal, but it simply gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Pendragon was the title for a chief king among the ancient British, borne by Uther, father of King Arthur.

clue.text: Mother bit old resistance fighter in ring

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a tad is a little bit
O is the abbreviation for old
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A mother bites a veteran Resistance fighter who has her surrounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like the past tense of bite; it is a noun meaning a small amount. 'Resistance fighter' splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who makes the final kill in a bullring arena.

clue.text: Lose millions on Scottish island

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for million
Islay is a Hebridean island famous for whisky

explanation.surface: Someone loses a fortune on a Scottish island venture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts M above the island.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it somewhere and forget where, so it is temporarily gone.

clue.text: Thanks boring Italian magistrate in advancing years

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: ta is British informal thanks
the doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa

explanation.surface: Gratitude towards a tedious Italian official who is growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the period of old age, often with a weakening of the mind, that comes with advancing years.

clue.text: Oscar studies European city

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a den is a private room for study
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Someone named Oscar is looking at a city on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European city' looks like the whole definition, but 'European' supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Odense is the third-largest Danish urban centre, on the island of Funen and the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen.

clue.text: Exchange these unusual plugs in kids' favourite store

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
a plug fills a hole, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
swop is a British variant spelling of swap

explanation.surface: A shop where children trade odd electrical plugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit inside SWOP, an older British spelling of swap. Sweets are what Americans call candy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet shop sells sweets, the British word for candy, so it is a confectionery store children love.

clue.text: A uniform state

blocks.note: a can mean per, as in twice a day
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A comment that the uniform is in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' looks like the article; it means per, as in 'ten pounds a head'. 'State' could be a condition, but it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation, and a state can mean a sovereign country.

clue.text: Some wine spilled over curvy figure

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, a run of letters inside
turned over means flipped, so the letters read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: read backwards, a run of letters spans the two words

explanation.surface: Wine slopped across a curvaceous figure, perhaps at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curvy figure' suggests a body; it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is a flattened circle, an oval geometric shape bounded by a smooth curved line.

clue.text: Vegetable is mostly fruit

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a fruit

explanation.surface: A claim that a vegetable is mostly fruit, as botanists say of tomatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: PEAR loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a small green seed eaten as a vegetable, though botanically it grows in a pod.

clue.text: Maybe opposed to firing West Indian, one ace quits

indicators.note: one that quits leaves, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: someone from Antigua, a Caribbean island
A is the card abbreviation for ace; one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: A cricket team sacks its West Indian ace bowler, who promptly resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing' suggests sacking, but here it is shooting guns. 'Maybe' signals that being against gunfire is just one way to be anti-gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-gun stance opposes firearms, so someone holding it might well be against shooting weapons.

clue.text: Rudely ran off in West End venue

indicators.note: something off is wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatregoer rudely storms out in the middle of a London show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rudely' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'off' does that job. The West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: The Theatre Royal, Drury Lane is a historic London playhouse, often just called by its street name.
